effect: The final result shows how touch signals and muscle commands work together to adjust grip and keep the glass steady.
reaction: The slipping-glass example makes the feedback loop concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile action: the slipping and correction panels connect skin sensation, nerves and muscle work to a familiar task.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the supporting and surface layers felt somewhat predictable, although the resulting cross-section helped explain how surface cells receive supplies.

surprise.text: I was interested that the outermost skin cells are dead while living layers beneath replace them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt without a clear purpose; the component names and pictures generally suggested how they fit together.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see another familiar action explained through connected body systems, though the assembly steps themselves were often predictable.
